title: Open Home Purchase Agreements per Buyer: The Two-Agreement Limit
content:
**Rule.** A buyer may have up to 2 Home Purchase Agreements open at once. An agreement is open while its status is pending ratification, ratified, under construction or closing scheduled; closed, cancelled and terminated agreements do not count. A new agreement is written only where the number of the buyer's open agreements, not counting the agreement being written, is below 2 before it is written. An agreement that would exceed the limit is not written.

**Basis of the count.** The count is taken from Calloway's agreement records for the same buyer (the buyer's customer record), as they stand before the new agreement is written. It is not taken from what the buyer says about other purchases.

## Desk reading of the limit

| Buyer's open Home Purchase Agreements before writing (agreement being written excluded) | Below 2? | Under this limit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Yes | The new agreement may be written |
| 1 | Yes | The new agreement may be written |
| 2 | No | The new agreement is not written |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical buyers)

- A hypothetical buyer with one agreement under construction and one agreement that closed last year has 1 open agreement; the closed one does not count, so the limit allows a new agreement.
- A hypothetical buyer with one agreement pending ratification and one closing scheduled has 2 open agreements; a third agreement would exceed the limit and is not written.
- A hypothetical buyer whose earlier agreement was cancelled and whose other agreement was terminated has 0 open agreements under this count.
